# NPM Improved v1.6.6 — NPMX node-aware Let's Encrypt validation

## Certificate issuance across NPMX
- Any node receiving an HTTP-01 validation request can now answer it: serve a local challenge token if present, otherwise ask its configured NPMX primary over the existing signed, replay-protected peer transport.
- Certificate requests initiated on secondary nodes continue to be processed by the authoritative primary through existing NPMX write arbitration.
- Bound token syntax and response payloads; return a clear unavailable response if the primary cannot be reached. Do not copy private keys or credential material to other nodes for challenge handling.

## Nginx and upgrade safety
- Route ACME challenge paths to the built-in local API without requiring external containers or services.
- Allow ACME requests through node-local Analytics Center blocking, but only for valid challenge-token paths.
- Include ACME handling on proxy, redirect and 404 hosts before any certificate is assigned.
- Automatically refresh persisted host configurations using validated Nginx transactions and rollback when old configurations still lack ACME support or contain outdated blocking expressions.
- Overlay the updated ACME Nginx location into the production image.

## Verification
- Backend CI and repository health checks passed.
- Required Checks passed, including production-container build and smoke test.
- Production deployment must update primary before secondaries and then verify an HTTP-01 token can be served by both public IPs before retrying certificate issuance.
